memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: You shall not give false testimony against your neighbor. - Deut 5:20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This command originally guarded the courtroom, where a false witness could destroy an innocent person's life or reputation with a lie. But its reach extends far beyond legal settings. It speaks against gossip, slander, twisting the truth, spreading rumours, and every word we use to damage another person. Our tongues carry the power to build up or to tear down, and God calls His people to be people of truth.

Words matter to God because He is a God of truth. He cannot lie (Titus 1:2). When we deceive, distort, or slander, we act against His very nature. When we speak truthfully — even when it costs us — we reflect the character of the One we belong to. In a world swimming in half-truths, spin, and careless words online, honest speech is a powerful witness.

Jesus called Himself "the truth" (John 14:6), and Satan the "father of lies" (John 8:44). Every time we choose honesty and refuse to tear others down, we stand on the side of Christ. And when we have failed with our words — as we all have — His grace covers us and His Spirit retrains our tongues. Ask God today to make your words true, kind, and used for building others up rather than tearing them down. Let people trust what you say because they know Whom you follow.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do my words consistently reflect truth, or do I bend it when convenient?
- Have I damaged anyone through gossip, rumour, or careless speech?
- How can I use my words this week to build others up rather than tear them down?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, You are the God of truth who cannot lie. Guard my tongue from falsehood and gossip, and make my words honest, kind, and used to build others up, so that they reflect Jesus who is the Truth. Amen.
